references.text: Moses describes how the Israelites took all the cities of Sihon and struck everyone with the ban, men, women, and children, but kept the livestock and plunder from the cities.
The Israelites did the same to Og, king of Bashan, striking all the inhabitants with the ban, but taking the livestock and plunder as war booty.
The law concerning war booty: the women, children, livestock, and everything else in the city could be taken as spoil, but the men were to be killed.
The Lord gave permission to the Israelites to take the spoil and livestock from Ai as war booty, unlike Jericho.
The Israelites took the livestock and plunder from Ai as war booty, just as the Lord had commanded Joshua.
Joshua captured Makkedah and struck all its inhabitants with the edge of the sword; no survivors were left.
Summary of Joshua's campaign in the south: he struck everything that breathed with the ban, just as the Lord had commanded.
The Israelites took the Midianite women, children, livestock, and all their goods as spoil and war plunder.
The previous verse describes how Joshua struck all the inhabitants of Hazor with the edge of the sword and left nothing that breathed alive.
